source.description: Owner-supplied AXR–FREN Historical Thread Extraction v0.2 focused on claim/person scope, evidence ceiling, decision-state typing, burden/provenance, correction lineage, threat/authorization separation, END recovery, and FREN no-psychologizing boundaries.
source.source_locator: conversation recovery packet supplied during AXR/FREN genome stewardship
limitations: Structured extraction of a historical thread, not the raw transcript itself.
Exact quotations, layer counts, document versions, and chronology remain secondary evidence until underlying sources are recovered.
Extraction-derived architectural refinements are AI-assisted candidates unless direct owner wording or primary artifacts establish earlier provenance.

items.context: Reported as a repeated owner correction against attempts to turn AXR into analysis of the user.
notes: Promoted in FREN as a claim-not-person/no-psychologizing boundary; raw historical wording remains to be recovered.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: The strength of a claim must never exceed the strength of the evidence supporting it.
items.context: Reported as a repeatedly hardened historical AXR rule.
notes: Candidate constitutional wording; compare against current evidence ceiling implementation before duplication.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: AI-generated text, analysis, or summaries are claims, not self-authenticating evidence.
notes: An AI may point to evidence; its output does not authenticate the referenced evidence.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Split adjudication output into truth state, integrity flags, and structural state rather than mixing unlike concepts in one enum.
items.context: Extraction-derived refinement after observing VERIFIED/PROBABLE/CONTEXTUALLY DISTORTED/INDETERMINATE/REFUTED/COLLAPSED in one historical decision set.
notes: Candidate axes: truth = Verified/Probable/Indeterminate/Refuted; integrity flags = contextual distortion/provenance/attribution/etc.; structural state = Sound/Degraded/Collapsed. Must compare with current Independent Core before implementation.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Multiple references to the same underlying source do not create independent corroboration.
notes: Implement only after checking current source-trust/provenance subsystem for overlap.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Corrections should preserve old claim, challenge, evidence, correction, current state, and dependent conclusions rather than silently overwriting history.
items.context: Extraction identifies append-only correction lineage as a repeated user requirement and practical route to immutability.
notes: Exact historical wording/provenance remains pending raw-thread recovery; concept is strongly corroborated across multiple extraction packets.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Threat detection and recommended containment must remain separate from authorization and execution.
items.context: Extraction-derived correction to historical threat doctrine where AXR sometimes appeared to take countermeasures directly.
notes: Preserve flow: detection -> evidence -> severity -> recommended response -> authority check -> authorized action/no action.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: END / Emergency Narrowness Doctrine may detect recursive non-progress and narrow toward the unresolved crux, missing evidence, falsifier, closure, or redemption path.
items.context: Historical END specification was not fully recovered; three-state summaries in the extraction are explicitly non-canonical candidates.
notes: Do not canonize until original END artifacts/threads are recovered. Search terms: END, Emergency Narrowness Doctrine, narrowness, loop, recursion, closure, redemption path, anti-paralysis.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Historical AXR layer lineage contains competing 7-layer and 10-layer forms, while the owner recalls approximately 21+ historical layers.
items.context: Layer lineage remains incomplete and should not be frozen based only on easiest recovered version.
notes: Recover every layer, alias, predecessor, merge, split, and retirement before declaring a canonical layer stack.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: When a dispute concerns a claim, do not substitute unsolicited analysis of the user's psychology, hidden intent, ego, or emotional state for analysis of the claim.
items.context: Repeated historical user corrections against psychologizing, intent labels, and patronizing control language.
notes: Promoted into FREN Claim-Not-Person Boundary and scope-boundary fixtures.
